{{nihongo|'''Takamahiko Shrine'''|高天彦神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Kitakubo, {{ill|Gose, Nara|Q847334|qid=Q847334}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and under the former {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=shrine ranking system}} it was a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. {{nihongo|'''Takamahiko Shrine'''|高天彦神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
The three enshrined deities are as follows{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1982}}.
* {{ill|Takamimusubi|lt=Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi-no-Kami}} (たかみむすびのかみ) - principal deity.
* {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}} (いちきしまひめのみこと)
* {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}}

In the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, the deity is listed as one seat. It is inferred that originally it enshrined the local land deity "Takamahiko"{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Gods)|1985}}.

The name "Takama" in the shrine/deity name is also a local place name. Since old times there has been a theory identifying this area with the legendary {{ill|Takamagahara|Q1141974|qid=Q1141974}}. Other theories say the name derives from a phonetic change of Takamimusubi's name, or that Takamimusubi had an alternate name "Takamahiko-no-Kami," or that "Takama" means "high flatland" on the mid-slope of Mt. Kongō{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1982}}. In the {{ill|Man'yōshū|Q834321|qid=Q834321}}, a well-known poem refers to "Takama of Katsuragi" (Book 7, poem 1337){{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Gods)|1985}}. In the Engishiki Jinmyōchō, Takama Kishino Shrine and Takamayama Satao Shrine are listed in Uchi District and are both identified with shrines on Mt. Kongō's mid-slope in {{ill|Gojō, Nara|Q602571|qid=Q602571}}, which has led to a theory that "Takamahiko-no-Kami" itself is the mountain spirit of Mt. Kongō{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Gods)|1985}}.

== History ==
== Overview ==
[[File:Takamahiko-jinja Shirakumo-dake.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Shirakumo-dake ({{ill|Sacred mountains|Q1595289|qid=Q1595289}})}}{{small|Takamahiko Shrine precinct at lower left.}}]]
Foundation is unknown. The shrine stands on the east foot of {{ill|Mount Kongō|Q1348310|qid=Q1348310|lt=Mt. Kongō}} and is said originally to have worshipped Shirakumo-dake (also Shirakumo peak, elevation 985 m) behind the shrine buildings as the sacred mountain<ref name="board">Explanatory board in precincts.</ref>{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}.

In the record for {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} 1 ({{ill|806|ab|806|af|806|als|806|am|806 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|806|ar|806|ary|806|ast|806|az|806|azb|۸۰۶ (میلادی)|bar|806|bcl|806|be|806|be_x_old|806|bg|806|bn|৮০৬|bpy|মারি ৮০৬|br|806|bs|806.|ca|806|cdo|806 nièng|ceb|806|ckb|٨٠٦|crh|806|cs|806|csb|806|cv|806|cy|806|da|806|de|806|el|806|eml|806|eo|806|es|806|et|806|eu|806|fa|۸۰۶ (میلادی)|fi|806|fo|806|fr|806|frr|806|fy|806|ga|806|gan|806年|gd|806|gl|806|he|806|hi|806|hr|806.|ht|806 (almanak jilyen)|hu|806|hy|806|id|806|ilo|806|io|806|is|806|it|806|ja|806年|jv|806|ka|806|kaa|806|kk|806 жыл|ko|806년|la|806|lb|806|lij|806|lmo|806|lt|806 m.|lv|806. gads|map_bms|806|mdf|806|mg|806|mhr|806|mk|806|mr|इ.स. ८०६|mrj|806 и|ms|806|mzn|۸۰۶|nah|806|nap|806|nds|806|new|सन् ८०६|nl|806|nn|806|no|806|nrm|806|nso|806|oc|806|or|୮୦୬|os|806-æм аз|pl|806|pt|806|qu|806|ro|806|ru|806 год|rue|806|sa|८०६|scn|806|sd|806ع|se|806|sh|806.|shn|806|si|806|sk|806|sl|806|smn|806|sq|806|sr|806|su|806|sv|806|sw|806|tg|Соли 806|th|พ.ศ. 1349|tk|806|tl|806|tly|806|tr|806|tt|806 ел|uk|806|ur|806ء|uz|806|vec|806|vi|806|vls|806|war|806|wuu|806年|xmf|806|zh|806年|zh_min_nan|806 nî|zh_yue|806年|qid=Q30021}}) in ''{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}}'', "Takamahiko deity, four households (in Yamato province, allocated in Hōki 10)" is recorded, indicating shrine households allocated from within Yamato in {{ill|Hōki|Q18520676|qid=Q18520676}} 10 ({{ill|779|Q31124|qid=Q31124}}){{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1982}}.

In the Six National Histories, in {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} 1 ({{ill|806|ab|806|af|806|als|806|am|806 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|806|ar|806|ary|806|ast|806|az|806|azb|۸۰۶ (میلادی)|bar|806|bcl|806|be|806|be_x_old|806|bg|806|bn|৮০৬|bpy|মারি ৮০৬|br|806|bs|806.|ca|806|cdo|806 nièng|ceb|806|ckb|٨٠٦|crh|806|cs|806|csb|806|cv|806|cy|806|da|806|de|806|el|806|eml|806|eo|806|es|806|et|806|eu|806|fa|۸۰۶ (میلادی)|fi|806|fo|806|fr|806|frr|806|fy|806|ga|806|gan|806年|gd|806|gl|806|he|806|hi|806|hr|806.|ht|806 (almanak jilyen)|hu|806|hy|806|id|806|ilo|806|io|806|is|806|it|806|ja|806年|jv|806|ka|806|kaa|806|kk|806 жыл|ko|806년|la|806|lb|806|lij|806|lmo|806|lt|806 m.|lv|806. gads|map_bms|806|mdf|806|mg|806|mhr|806|mk|806|mr|इ.स. ८०६|mrj|806 и|ms|806|mzn|۸۰۶|nah|806|nap|806|nds|806|new|सन् ८०६|nl|806|nn|806|no|806|nrm|806|nso|806|oc|806|or|୮୦୬|os|806-æм аз|pl|806|pt|806|qu|806|ro|806|ru|806 год|rue|806|sa|८०६|scn|806|sd|806ع|se|806|sh|806.|shn|806|si|806|sk|806|sl|806|smn|806|sq|806|sr|806|su|806|sv|806|sw|806|tg|Соли 806|th|พ.ศ. 1349|tk|806|tl|806|tly|806|tr|806|tt|806 ел|uk|806|ur|806ء|uz|806|vec|806|vi|806|vls|806|war|806|wuu|806年|xmf|806|zh|806年|zh_min_nan|806 nî|zh_yue|806年|qid=Q30021}}), "Takamahiko deity" at Senior Fourth Rank Upper is said to have received regular seasonal offerings by wish of Princess Yoshino Daikō ({{ill|Princess Inoe|Q7244649|qid=Q7244649}}), though the relation between the princess and this shrine is unclear{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Gods)|1985}}. Later, in {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 6 ({{ill|839|Q23874|qid=Q23874}}), it is recorded that "Takamahiko deity" at Junior Third Rank entered the myojin register; in {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} 3 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), it was promoted to Junior Second Rank, Second Merit Grade{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1982}}.

In the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it is listed in Katsuragi-kami District of Yamato as "Takamahiko Shrine, myojin major, receiving offerings at monthly, aidame, and niiname rites," and is recorded as receiving court offerings for {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}}, {{ill|Ainame Festival|Q11581944|qid=Q11581944}}, and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}}{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1982}}.

Subsequent history is unclear. Because Takama is a trailhead to Mt. Kongō, it is said that literati and haiku poets visited along with the growth of Katsuragi Shugendō, and the shrine was also called "Hikosawa Gongen"{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1982}}. On the east side of the shrine there was also Takama-dera, a {{ill|Jingū-ji|fr|Jingū-ji|it|Jingū-ji|ja|神宮寺|pl|Jingū-ji|ru|Дзингудзи|zh|神宮寺|qid=Q1074971}}{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Gods)|1985}}.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} under the modern shrine ranking system{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The current honden was completed in Meiji 10 ({{ill|1877|Q7773|qid=Q7773}}). At completion it had a thatched roof; in Shōwa 52 ({{ill|1977|Q2481|qid=Q2481}}) it was re-roofed with {{ill|Sekishū-gawara|Q11586446|qid=Q11586446}}, and in Reiwa 1 ({{ill|2019|Q25274|qid=Q25274}}) again re-roofed with galvalume steel panels.
